table_description: Project master for the SAMPLE schema. One row per project with its name, the owning department, the responsible employee, planned staffing in person-months, planned start and end dates, and an optional parent project. Projects form a tree via the self-referential MAJPROJ column.
use_cases: List projects owned by a given department
Look up the responsible employee for a project
Walk the project hierarchy via MAJPROJ (sub-projects under a major project)
Filter projects by planned timeframe (PRSTDATE, PRENDATE) — e.g. projects ending this year
Roll up planned staffing (PRSTAFF) by department or major project
data_quality_notes: PROJNO is CHAR(6); compare with string literals like 'AD3100', not integers.
DEPTNO is CHAR(3) and is the foreign key to DEPARTMENT.DEPTNO — both are strings.
RESPEMP is CHAR(6) matching EMPLOYEE.EMPNO and is NOT NULL — every project has a responsible employee.
MAJPROJ is self-referential: it points at another PROJECT.PROJNO. Top-level projects have MAJPROJ NULL.
PRSTAFF is DECIMAL(5,2) and may be NULL for projects whose staffing wasn't planned at the column-level.
PRSTDATE / PRENDATE are planned dates, not actuals — actual activity dates live in EMP_ACT.EMSTDATE / EMENDATE.

table_columns.name: DEPTNO
table_columns.description: Owning department. Foreign key to DEPARTMENT.DEPTNO.

table_columns.name: RESPEMP
table_columns.description: Employee responsible for the project. Foreign key to EMPLOYEE.EMPNO.

table_columns.name: MAJPROJ
table_columns.description: Parent (major) project. Self-referential foreign key to PROJECT.PROJNO — top-level projects have this NULL.
